messages:
alex: heads-up — PR 18299 just failed the CI microbench for kernel-selector. threshold diff +14% median latency on kernel_selector_v2, blocking merge :rotating_light:
bench-bot: automated summary:
  suite: perf/unit/kernel_selector
  baseline: 0.98 ms median
  current: 1.12 ms median
  delta: +14.3% (threshold 7%)
  diff: https://ci.internal/reports/18299/kernel_selector/diff
ci-bot: test run id 9e4c — artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-ci/perf/18299/
mira: ew. earliest suspect is the batching-timer tweak in commit a1b2c3f (batcher: coarsen sample timer). that touched the sampler and the fallback path for small batches, could change kernel affinity.
devin: +1 to bisect. i'll run a quick local microbench. command i'm using: `./tools/perf_run --suite perf/unit/kernel_selector --seed 42 --runs 20`
alex: please also capture flamegraph + kvcache hitrate. last time a timer change shifted small-batch behavior and dropped KV hitrate for prefix-heavy traces.
devin: ran locally, reproduces roughly: baseline 0.95 -> PR 1.10. attached flamegraph gist: https://gist.github.com/devin/ff2d4 (shows extra time in batch_coalesce and kernel_select())
bench-bot: per-run breakdown (sample from CI artifacts):
  - kernel_select: +9.1%
  - batch_coalesce: +18%
  - kv_cache_lookup: -1.2% (noise)
  - tail latency p95: +21%
sam: adding context — PR touched `batcher/sampler.rs` and `runtime/kernel_selector.rs`. suspect interaction where sampler returns slightly later sequences causing different kernel path to be chosen (small kernel vs fused kernel).
mira: i reproduced with `--seq-len 64` and the selector flips to small-kernel path. the small-kernel path is slower for this model/seqlen combo after commit because we changed prefetch ordering.
alex: can we run a targeted bisect to narrow to commit? devin, can you run `git bisect` across the PR series or revert the batching-timer change temporarily for the CI job?
devin: starting quick bisect now across the 6 commits in the PR branch, will run 8x microbench runs each. queueing in my workstation.
ci-bot: note: rollout blocked flag set on PR 18299 by merge-gate automation. Will not auto-merge until resolved.
mira: alternative mitigation — pin kernel selector to previous heuristic via flag: `REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR=stable` in the container, then re-run CI. if that fixes we can keep PR but gate the sampler change behind runtime flag + perf test.
alex: good call. but given this is a merge-to-main perf delta we should either revert the single commit that regressed or flip the runtime flag immediately. which is faster?
devin: bisect results: commit a1b2c3f is the regressing commit — removing that delta restores baseline in local microbench. pushing a revert PR now: #18301.
bench-bot: PR 18301 created: revert(batch): coarsen sample timer (a1b2c3f) — triggering CI perf run.
alex: sounds good. hold rollout until CI green with revert. also add a follow-up to add a perf-unit test that covers this seq-len/kernel selector boundary.
mira: i'll draft the perf test (seqlen sweep) and add it to the golden suite. also will add an integration check for kv hitrate regressions on small-batch traces.
ci-bot: CI perf run for PR 18301 completed: kernel_selector median 0.99 ms, delta vs baseline +1%. artifacts: https://ci.internal/reports/18301/kernel_selector
alex: revert CI green, unblocking PR 18299. thanks all — please follow up with a clean rework of sampler that preserves kernel-affinity. :thumbsup:
